title: Mineral balm dragged over wet slate

tokens.v: Full-bleed photograph filling the entire frame edge to edge with no border, frame, letterbox band or matte of any kind. EXTREME MACRO, no body or hands anywhere in frame: one thick chalk-white swipe of the mineral balm dragged the full width of a rain-wet split slate tile, its leading edge ploughed into a standing ridge with fine combing behind where the oval rim cut it, the balm dense and matte against stone that stays black and mirror-wet either side. The tube lies on its side at the end of the drag, cap off and out of frame, the balm dome shaved flat where it did the work. 100mm macro at f/5.6, framed 1:1 life-size, camera twenty degrees off the slate plane, one hard raking key from the left so the ridge throws a long shadow and the wet stone fires a single specular band across the bottom third. CAIRN stands embossed in relief along the flank, struck up out of the aluminium and left inkless, the raking key lighting the top edge of every letter and pooling shadow below it. The near slate is left bare and empty to the bottom edge.
